A developer’s assistant may need a specialist report. The intended AegisPay flow lets it choose useful data while trusted tools enforce the accepted price, task budget and wallet policy.

Illustrative scenario · not executed

“Review the fictional demo-parser dependency for a basic release triage note. Buy only what’s needed, within 0.10 Testnet XLM.”

No report was purchased in this example. The recorded authorization above does not establish a QuickSignal purchase or report delivery.

Permission is only
part of the proof.
The model proposes. Rules decide.
A per-payment cap, finite escrow and an application task budget are separate controls. A cap is not a daily on-chain budget.
Authorization comes before claim.
Verified authorization credits merchant-pending escrow. A separate merchant claim moves it out of pending.
Uncertainty keeps its identity.
An unknown result stays unresolved. Observe the saved operation; never sign or submit another payment to clear a timeout.

Current public mode: recorded integration proof. The full model purchase, protected report delivery and live product console still require their release gates.
